transcript.content: Hello, I’m Dr. ____. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Well, what really brought me in is... I've been having this issue when people are talking to me. Like, my wife will be telling me about my cousin’s appointments or his rides, and I’m looking right at her while she speaks. But a minute later, I realize I didn’t actually take in half of what she just said. I figured I should probably come in and talk to someone about it.
Do you often have trouble focusing or staying attentive during ordinary conversations?

Yeah, that's exactly it. Like I was just saying, it happens during totally normal chats. My wife will be going over my cousin's appointments or who's giving him a ride, and I'm looking right at her... but it just doesn't register. A minute later I realize I missed half of what she told me. So, yes, staying focused just listening to people is definitely the main issue.
Do you also miss or lose track of information when you are reading?

Yeah, it definitely happens with reading, too. If I sit down to work out a catering order, or... or even if I'm listening through a parish planning call, I usually start off fine. But before long, my mind just wanders. I'll realize I have to go back over the exact same notes because it's like I never even read them in the first place.
Have you had trouble paying attention like this since childhood?

Yes, I have. Even way back in grade school, well before I was 12, my teachers used to tell my parents that I was a bright kid, but I was just always daydreaming. I'd end up leaving my homework inside my desk, and... I just always needed reminders to actually finish my classwork. So, yeah, it's been an issue since I was young.
Do you also have trouble with organization or finishing tasks at work or home?

Yeah, finishing things can definitely be an issue. I’ll begin something really simple, like setting up my cousin’s pill organizer, or... or just cleaning off the prep table after I'm done cooking. But then I'll notice later on that I left one or two steps totally unfinished. I just sort of move on before the job is actually complete.

latest_inference.note: Symptoms began in childhood, occur across settings, and include inattention, distractibility, and unfinished tasks, which strongly supports childhood-onset hyperkinetic disorder/ADHD inattentive presentation. This rules out primary generalized anxiety, depression, or auditory processing disorder as the main explanation.
